name: Jehoshaphat (son of Asa)
title: Judah's Reformer King
summary: Jehoshaphat was the fourth king of Judah after the kingdom split and reigned for 25 years. He is known for his religious reforms, his organization of the judicial system, and his trust in God when facing hostile armies. Despite his piety, he was criticized for his alliances with the wicked northern kingdom of Israel.

keyEvents.title: Religious Reforms in Judah
keyEvents.description: Jehoshaphat sent officials, Levites and priests to teach the people the law of the Lord throughout all the cities of Judah.

keyEvents.title: Alliance with Ahab against Aram
keyEvents.description: Jehoshaphat made an alliance with Ahab king of Israel and went with him to war against Ramoth in Gilead, despite the warning of the prophet Micaiah.

keyEvents.title: Victory over Moab and Ammon through Praise
keyEvents.description: When a great army from Moab, Ammon and Edom threatened Judah, Jehoshaphat sought the Lord. God gave them victory without battle as the Levites praised, and the enemies destroyed each other.

keyEvents.title: Organization of the Judicial System
keyEvents.description: Jehoshaphat appointed judges in all the fortified cities of Judah and established a higher court in Jerusalem with priests, Levites and family heads.

keyEvents.title: The Prophet Jehu's Rebuke
keyEvents.description: After Jehoshaphat returned from the war with Ahab, the prophet Jehu met him and rebuked him for helping the wicked and loving those who hated the Lord.

keyEvents.title: Failed Merchant Fleet with Ahaziah
keyEvents.description: Jehoshaphat built ships together with Ahaziah king of Israel to sail to Tarshish, but the ships were wrecked because he had allied himself with a wicked king.
